paper_id: Frequency Matching in Spiking Neural Networks for mmWave Sensing
title: Frequency Matching in Spiking Neural Networks for mmWave Sensing
venue: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning
motivation: ANNs need heavy preprocessing/deep architecture for mmWave edge sensing, conflicting with efficiency constraints
problem_framing: Mechanism-data alignment: connect LIF temporal filtering with mmWave spectral structure
key_insight: Match LIF effective bandwidth to discriminative spectral content to suppress noise while preserving signal
method_signature: Frequency-Matching Score (FMS) for β selection via maximum-deviation rule on FMS curve
evaluation_criteria: Test accuracy, energy consumption, latency across edge devices on 4 mmWave datasets
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: β† marks onset of over-low-pass behavior, not optimal β; more complex LIF variants hurt cross-dataset consistency
evidence_for_taste: it remains unclear when and why SNNs are advantageous
hard thresholding indiscriminately suppressing both noise and informative components
costly dataset-specific sweeps and offers limited mechanistic insight
accuracy degradations are empirically more frequent
more flexible neuron dynamics may increase representational capacity
their accuracy varies substantially across datasets
thinking_moves: 把SNN优势问题从经验现象重新frame成可解释的mechanism-data alignment
避开调参式β优化，改用几何构造定义reference boundary
用频域分析把感知问题转化为频率选择问题
用IIR低通滤波等价性把神经动力学映射到频谱响应
对比硬阈值低通与软低通保留高频信息的差异
